hero.oneLiner: India's largest and oldest asset management company by mutual fund QAAUM (₹12,509.98 billion, 15.3% market share as at March 31, 2026), acting as investment manager to SBI Mutual Fund under dual parentage of State Bank of India and Amundi.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's largest and oldest asset management company by mutual fund QAAUM (₹12,509.98 billion, 15.3% market share as at March 31, 2026), acting as investment manager to SBI Mutual Fund under dual parentage of State Bank of India and Amundi.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SBI Funds Management Limited is the investment manager to SBI Mutual Fund, which commenced operations in June 1987 as the first mutual fund entity outside the Unit Trust of India. It manages 128 mutual fund schemes across equity and equity-oriented, debt, arbitrage, ETFs, index and overseas fund-of-funds, and liquid and overnight categories, serving a unique investor base of 18.00 million individuals and institutions as of March 31, 2026. Beyond mutual funds it offers Portfolio Management Services and advisory mandates (together "Alternates"), alternative investment funds (AIFs), specialised investment funds (SIFs), and India-focused offshore/UCITS mandates for overseas institutional investors.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- SBI Mutual Fund — Fund managed - the Company acts as its investment manager: Commenced operations in June 1987 as the first mutual fund entity outside the Unit Trust of India; all AUM/QAAUM/MAAUM references in the RHP refer to SBI Mutual Fund
- SBI Funds International (IFSC) Limited — Entity listed under the other directorships (unlisted public companies) of Managing Director and CEO Debasish Mishra: The routed extract does not expressly state the relationship of this entity to the Company; the RHP elsewhere refers to "Subsidiaries" of the Company
- Amundi Asset Management — Promoter; parent of Amundi India Holding: Headquartered in Paris and listed on Euronext, Paris; close to €2.4 trillion AUM, 200 million+ retail clients, 5,400 employees across 34 countries including 905 investment professionals, and 1,000 institutional and corporate clients as at March 31, 2026
- Société Générale Asset Management S.A. — Former joint venture partner: Acquired a 37% stake in the Company in 2004; shareholding passed to Amundi India Holding after the 2011 merger of Crédit Agricole's and Société Générale's asset management businesses
- Corporate Debt Market Development Fund (CDMDF) — Specialised AIF for which the Company was appointed sponsor and investment manager in 2023: Established following the Union Budget 2022 announcement to create a permanent institutional framework in the corporate bond market; designed to instil confidence during stress and enhance secondary market liquidity
- Group Companies (unnamed in the routed extract) — Group Companies of the Company: Stated absence: as on the date of the RHP there is no pending litigation involving the Group Companies which may have a material impact on the Company

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Mutual Fund (128 schemes):** Equity and equity-oriented schemes, Debt / fixed income schemes, Arbitrage schemes, ETFs, Index funds, Overseas fund-of-funds, Liquid and overnight schemes
- **Alternates:** Portfolio Management Services (PMS), Advisory mandates, Alternative Investment Funds (AIF), Corporate Debt Market Development Fund (CDMDF) - sponsor and investment manager since 2023
- **Specialised:** Specialized Investment Funds (SIF)
- **International / offshore:** India-focused investment management mandates for overseas institutional investors (Japan, Australia, Korea), UCITS India-focused funds sponsored by Amundi (₹107,834.60 million), Advisory services to Amundi's Global Emerging Markets mandates (₹149,653.07 million of India-related assets under advisory), SBI International Access - US Equity Fund of Funds (in partnership with Amundi group)
- **Digital platforms / facilities:** InvesTap mutual fund mobile application, Jan Nivesh SIP facility (daily investments from ₹250, launched February 2025), Partner (B2B application), Mitra (B2B application), Mutual fund investing integrated into SBI's YONO digital banking platform

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Not a manufacturing issuer - there is no physical supply chain. The equivalent vertical structure is distribution and parentage. The Company is the investment manager to SBI Mutual Fund (India's oldest AMC lineage; SBI Mutual Fund commenced operations in June 1987 as the first mutual fund entity outside the Unit Trust of India) and operates a pan-India omnichannel distribution model integrating physical and digital platforms. Third-party distribution as at March 31, 2026 comprised 132,519 institutional and individual mutual fund distributors (MFDs), including 122,460 independent financial advisors (IFAs), 9,964 national distributors (NDs) and 95 banks (including SBI); the DRHP does not print a direct-versus-distributor or channel-wise percentage split of AUM or revenue. Digital distribution runs through integration of mutual fund investment capabilities into SBI's YONO digital banking platform (100+ million YONO users as at March 31, 2026) and the proprietary InvesTap mobile application, which had 3.97 million registered users, 3.39 million active users, a 57.17% activation rate and 5.8 million downloads as at March 31, 2026; specialized B2B applications 'Partner' and 'Mitra' support the distributor network. Dual promoter parentage is presented as the structural distribution advantage: State Bank of India (established 1806; total assets of ₹ 83,215.7 billion, 23,265 branches and over 530 million customers as of March 31, 2026, and 246 international touch points across 29 countries) and Amundi (Amundi India Holding, a wholly owned subsidiary of Amundi Asset Management; Amundi group has close to €2.4 trillion of assets under management, more than 200 million retail clients, 5,400 employees across 34 countries including 905 investment professionals, and 1,000 institutional and corporate clients as at March 31, 2026, with approximately €543.00 billion in ETF AUM), providing access to Amundi's global distribution network across Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Scale economics are stated as operating expenses of 0.08% of QAAUM for Fiscal 2026, described as the lowest among the top 10 AMCs in India, against a range of 0.10% to 0.25% for the remaining top 10 AMCs in the same period (Source: CRISIL Report). Stated operating margin (revenue from operations less operating expenses, divided by total QAAUM of mutual fund and AIF) was 0.27% (FY26), 0.25% (FY25) and 0.21% (FY24); excluding passives it was 0.37% (FY26), 0.35% (FY25) and 0.30% (FY24). Ownership history: incorporated in 1992, received SEBI approval to act as asset manager to SBI Mutual Fund in 1993, became a joint venture in 2004 when Societe Generale Asset Management S.A. acquired a 37% stake, with Amundi India Holding succeeding to that shareholding following the 2011 merger of Credit Agricole's and Societe Generale's asset management businesses.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue and profitability are directly linked to QAAUM, since management fee income is levied on assets under management
- Product mix is a fee-realisation lever: equity-oriented and actively managed schemes carry higher management fee rates than debt-oriented schemes and passive funds (index funds/ETFs), so a shift toward lower-fee products reduces weighted average management fee realisation even if absolute QAAUM is stable or growing
- Operating leverage from a substantially fixed short-to-medium-term cost base - employee costs, technology infrastructure, regulatory compliance costs and distribution support - which amplifies both upside from scale and downside from any QAAUM decline
- Cost efficiency at scale: operating expenses at 0.08% of QAAUM for Fiscal 2026, the lowest among the top 10 AMCs (peer range 0.10%-0.25%)
- Operating margin measured against QAAUM improved from 0.21% (Fiscal 2024) to 0.27% (Fiscal 2026), and excluding passives from 0.30% to 0.37% - showing that passives dilute blended margin
- Profit after tax margin expanded from 60.50% in Fiscal 2024 to 61.65% in Fiscal 2026 on revenue from operations growth driven by increased asset management fees
- Cash generation: operating cash flow conversion of 69.39%, 78.44% and 81.10% of profit after tax in Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026 respectively
- Asset mix as at March 31, 2026: PMS and Advisory is the largest block at 57.29% of total QAAUM, mutual funds 42.46% and offshore schemes 0.02%; within total QAAUM, equity/equity-oriented/equity-hybrid (ex-arbitrage) is 18.06% and ETFs/index funds 13.76%
- The MD&A section 'Significant Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations' was truncated in the routed extract, so the Company's own enumerated MD&A drivers could not be captured

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Operate a dual capability that enables outbound diversification for domestic investors while attracting inbound global capital, positioning the Company to serve evolving investor preferences across geographies
- Maintain an international distribution presence in the Middle East and leverage SBI's and Amundi's global networks to serve customers across key international markets
- Continue an omnichannel distribution approach that integrates physical and digital platforms, including embracing digital channels to serve digitally native investors
- Deepen penetration in B-30 / tier 2 and tier 3 cities through the retail-focused distribution strategy
- Democratize access to mutual fund investing for first-time and small-ticket investors through the Jan Nivesh SIP facility (daily investments from ₹250), integrated across the InvesTap app and the Company's website
- Operate as a multi-style asset manager offering growth-oriented, value-oriented and quantitative investment strategies across product categories so investors can access varied investment philosophies
- Apply an investment approach combining top-down macroeconomic analysis with bottom-up fundamental research in equities and a safety-liquidity-returns framework in fixed income emphasising credit assessment and duration management
- Support investor acquisition through comprehensive investor education initiatives including in-person awareness programmes and active social media engagement (over one million followers/subscribers as at March 31, 2026)
- Achieve the benefits of listing the Equity Shares on the Stock Exchanges, which the Company expects will enhance its visibility and brand image and provide a public market for the Equity Shares in India

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As an asset manager the Company has no plants or manufacturing capacity; its expansion narrative is distribution, product and geographic rather than physical. Domestically it is widening a pan-India omnichannel footprint - 132,519 MFDs (122,460 IFAs, 9,964 NDs, 95 banks including SBI), integration of mutual fund capability into SBI's YONO platform, the proprietary InvesTap app (5.8 million downloads, 3.97 million registered users) and B2B apps Partner and Mitra - with an explicit push into B-30 / tier 2 and tier 3 cities, where B-30 MAAUM of ₹2,772.77 billion is 22.82% of mutual fund MAAUM and 65.16% of SIP count originates. Product expansion is visible in the launch of the Jan Nivesh SIP facility in February 2025 (daily investing from ₹250) and in Specialized Investment Funds (SIF), which contributed QAAUM of ₹29.95 billion as at March 31, 2026 against nil in the two prior years, alongside AIF QAAUM growth to ₹65.65 billion and the 2023 appointment as sponsor and investment manager of the CDMDF. Internationally the Company maintains a distribution presence in the Middle East, runs India-focused mandates for institutional investors in Japan, Australia and Korea, manages Amundi-sponsored UCITS India-focused funds of ₹107,834.60 million distributed across Europe, Middle East, South America and Southeast Asia, advises ₹149,653.07 million of Amundi Global Emerging Markets India-related assets, and facilitates outbound diversification for Indian investors (US$0.99 billion invested outside India through domestic funds as of March 31, 2026).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest AMC in India by mutual fund QAAUM - ₹12,509.98 billion and 15.3% market share as at March 31, 2026, a position consistently held since March 2021 (Source: CRISIL Report)
- India's largest passive (ETF and index funds) asset manager - passive QAAUM of ₹4,055.26 billion, 27.9% market share as at March 31, 2026, leadership held since March 2021
- Ranked 1st in B-30 locations with a 19.2% share of industry B-30 MAAUM, and 1st in PMS with a 39.7% market share as of March 31, 2026
- Strategic dual parentage - State Bank of India (India's largest bank by advances, deposits and branch network; ₹83,215.7 billion total assets, 23,265 branches, 530+ million customers) and Amundi (Europe's largest asset manager, global top 10) - described as a unique competitive advantage versus standalone domestic and other bank-affiliated AMCs
- Lowest operating expense ratio among the top 10 AMCs in India - operating expenses at 0.08% of QAAUM for Fiscal 2026 versus a 0.10%-0.25% range for the remaining top 10 AMCs
- Market-leading SIP franchise - 16.21 million live SIPs as of March 31, 2026; the RHP states a market share of 11.4% in "Our Business" and approximately 15.5% by live SIP count in "Basis for Offer Price" (both attributed to CRISIL Report, page 176; the two figures as printed are inconsistent and are recorded verbatim)
- Deep pan-India omnichannel distribution - 132,519 institutional and individual MFDs comprising 122,460 IFAs, 9,964 NDs and 95 banks (including SBI) as of March 31, 2026
- Large retail franchise with deep B-30 penetration - 17.95 million individual investors; 65.16% of SIP count originates from B-30 cities (excluding SIF)
- Proprietary digital distribution - InvesTap app with 3.97 million registered users, 3.39 million active users, 57.17% activation rate and 5.8 million downloads as at March 31, 2026, plus integration into SBI's YONO platform and B2B apps Partner and Mitra
- Scale research platform - dedicated research teams actively covering over 450 companies (over 85% of the BSE 500 by market capitalisation) and over 250 fixed income issuers as at March 31, 2026
- India's oldest AMC and first-mover on governance standards - first Indian AMC to comply with the CFA Institute's Asset Manager Code (2015) and to achieve full GIPS compliance (2020)
- Capital-efficient, cash-generative model - return on equity of 43.02% in Fiscal 2026 and operating cash flow conversion of 81.10% of profit after tax

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Revenues and profitability are directly linked to QAAUM (Internal Risk Factor 1) — Any decline in QAAUM, whether from market depreciation, investor redemptions or other factors, directly reduces management fee income, which is the Company's core revenue engine.
- Fixed cost base creates disproportionate profit sensitivity to a QAAUM decline — A significant portion of operating expenses - employee costs, technology infrastructure, regulatory compliance and distribution support - is relatively fixed in the short to medium term, so any material decline in QAAUM-linked revenues could disproportionately hit profitability.
- Adverse shift in QAAUM composition toward lower-fee products — Management fees vary significantly by category; equity-oriented and actively managed schemes earn higher fee rates than debt-oriented and passive funds. A mix shift to passives or debt, driven by investor preference, market conditions or regulation, would cut weighted average fee realisation and reduce revenue and profitability even with no fall in absolute QAAUM. This is structurally live given passives are already ₹4,055.26 billion (13.76% of total QAAUM) and the Company is the largest passive manager in India.
- Large-scale redemption risk, particularly from institutional investors and HNIs — Investor redemptions in response to poor scheme performance, market volatility or changing investor preferences could cause a significant QAAUM decline; the RHP singles out large-scale redemptions by institutional investors or high-net-worth individuals.
- Concentration of total QAAUM in PMS and Advisory mandates — PMS and Advisory account for ₹16,878.99 billion, or 57.29% of total QAAUM as at March 31, 2026 - a larger block than the mutual fund business (42.46%) - so the AUM headline is dominated by a mandate-driven business. (Composition is stated in the RHP; the RHP text supplied does not itself frame this concentration as a risk factor.)
- Reliance on a commissioned third-party industry report — Industry and market data throughout the RHP is derived from the CRISIL Intelligence report "Assessment of Mutual Fund Industry in India" dated July 2026, which was commissioned and exclusively paid for by the Company pursuant to an engagement letter dated February 16, 2026 and prepared exclusively in connection with the Offer; the RHP carries a dedicated risk factor on this at page 60.
- Inconsistent disclosure of SIP market share within the RHP — "Our Business" states 16.21 million live SIPs represent a market share of 11.4% as of March 31, 2026, while "Basis for Offer Price" states the same 16.21 million live SIPs represent approximately 15.5% by SIP count - both citing CRISIL Report page 176. One of the two figures must be wrong; a post-listing reader should treat the SIP share claim as unverified.
